Result rc=1, 'REFUSING to install', and the ledger's mtime afterwards is 1791095460 -- rewritten by step 1 (install.sh:723 'bd sync --flush-only') before refuse_below_floor is reached at :765.

ALREADY FILED FOR THE OTHER TWO CARRIERS: claude-workflow-plugin-tg72 (R5-F6, widened by R6-F5) covers README:300-302 and CHANGELOG:176. The commit message is a THIRD carrier that no prior round named.

THE INSTALLER'S OWN WORDING IS NOT THE FINDING and I am not widening it to one: refuse_below_floor's header (install.sh:561-566) names both the mkdir and the opt-in re-flush itself, the opt-in arm prints 'No plugin file has been written', and the non-opt-in arm prints 'Nothing has been written. findings.evidence:
NON-BLOCKING, v5.0.1 hardening. Not a PROSE finding and not BEHAVIOUR in any environment this project runs in -- see the scope note at the end, which is why it is medium and not high.

bd_canary_digest tries sha256sum, then shasum, and RETURNS EMPTY if neither resolves. bd_canary_fingerprint then still prints one '<path> ' line per watched path, which is non-empty, so the arm block's '[ -z "$BD_FP_BEFORE" ]' guard does not fire: BD_CANARY_ARMED=1 and the runner prints 'BD-CANARY: ARMED -- tracking N bd binary/binaries; a spec that rewrites one fails, by name'. Every subsequent per-spec comparison is then empty-digest versus empty-digest and can never differ.

MEASURED, not read. I extracted both functions VERBATIM from the shipped runner (awk on their own definitions) and ran them under env -i with HOME redirected and a PATH containing sort, cut, awk, sed and dirname plus a fake bd, but NOT sha256sum and NOT shasum. Output: 'digest tool on PATH: sha256sum=NONE shasum=NONE'; 'fingerprint (quoted): [<path>/bd ]' -> non-empty, so the arm block would set ARMED=1; then the watched binary was overwritten with a different script and the fingerprint re-sampled: byte-identical. 'VERDICT: canary would NOT trip on a real replacement (ARMED but blind)'.

PRECEDENT IN THIS SAME REPO, which is what makes this a divergence rather than a preference: .claude/scripts/workflow-manifest.sh:187-194 has a THREE-tool chain (sha256sum -> shasum -> openssl) and then die 'no usable sha256 tool on PATH (need sha256sum, shasum, or openssl)'. It fails CLOSED. The new canary fails OPEN, and the thing it announces while blind is detection.

SCOPE, STATED SO THIS IS NOT READ AS WORSE THAN IT IS: no lane and no documented host of this project lacks both tools. macOS ships shasum and ubuntu images ship sha256sum; on this host the canary armed correctly and runner-completeness section 14 passed all 14 legs including the 14.C1/14.C2 restore control (rc=0, 478 assertions). The gap is reachable only on a host where the rest of the harness would also be degraded.

UNVERIFIED SUGGESTION -- verify before adoption: add 'openssl dgst -sha256' as a third arm, and when no digest tool resolves set BD_CANARY_DISARM_REASON and DISARM rather than arming with empty digests.
findings.description: The BD-CANARY announces ARMED and cannot detect anything when neither sha256sum nor shasum is on PATH, because an empty digest compares equal to an empty digest. Its sibling helper in the same repo has a wider tool chain and dies instead. A guard that fails open while printing that it is armed is the failure mode this release exists to remove, in miniature.

findings.evidence:
NON-BLOCKING, v5.0.1 hardening. New code in this change set.

bd_canary_fingerprint watches THREE default locations: "$HOME/.local/bin/bd", "/usr/local/bin/bd", "/opt/homebrew/bin/bd" (:2064). The arm guard tests only TWO of them plus PATH: 'if ! command -v bd && [ ! -f "$HOME/.local/bin/bd" ] && [ ! -f /usr/local/bin/bd ]' (:2075). /opt/homebrew/bin/bd is absent from the guard.

CONSEQUENCE: on a host where bd exists ONLY at /opt/homebrew/bin/bd and is not on PATH, the canary DISARMS with 'no bd binary found on PATH or at either default install location' -- while the fingerprint it would have taken is non-empty and would have worked. The printed reason says 'either', consistent with the guard's two, but the code in fact watches three, so the message cannot name the location that was actually present.

VERIFIED BY READING ONLY, and deliberately not probed: the condition needs a Homebrew bd that is not on PATH, which is not this host's state (type -aP bd -> /Users/edk0/.local/bin/bd; the runner printed 'tracking 1 bd binary/binaries'). It fails LOUDLY (a printed DISARM line), not silently, which is why this is low.
findings.description: The BD-CANARY's arm guard checks two of the three default install locations its own fingerprint watches, so a Homebrew-only bd that is off PATH disarms the canary unnecessarily and the printed reason cannot name it.

findings.evidence:
NON-BLOCKING OBSERVATION, v5.0.1. EXPLICITLY NOT CAUSED BY THIS CANDIDATE -- the attribution was measured, not assumed.

MEASURED HERE: SPEC_TIMEOUT_S=3600 bash .claude/scripts/tests/run-tests.sh --filter runner-completeness -> rc=0, '--- runner-completeness.test.sh: PASSED (478 assertion(s) in 924s) ---'. 924s exceeds the default SPEC_TIMEOUT_S=900, and run-tests.sh's own header says a timeout is a FAILURE with a distinct reason, never a pass. So at defaults this spec times out on this macOS host, which is the host CLAUDE.md documents 'make test' being run on.

ATTRIBUTION A/B: I replicated section 14's fixture verbatim from the spec source (fake bd at 1.1.2 under a redirected HOME, aaa-bdwriter overwriting it, zzz-witness after it, BRE filter) and timed the two nested run-tests.sh --filter invocations the section performs: 1s for the trip run, 1s for the restore-control run, 2s total -- with the trip firing ('BD-CANARY TRIPPED' present) and the control clean. Section 14 is appended after section 13, so the candidate's contribution is ~2s of 924s. The overrun pre-exists it. The container figure for the same 478 assertions is 572s (commit message), so this is a host property, not content.

METHOD CAVEAT, stated because the two numbers are NOT directly comparable: my 924s is run-tests.sh's own per-spec timer -- the quantity the cap actually compares against -- under light concurrent load from this review session. The ledger's figures (756.16s / 771.35s for unrecorded-review-artifact.test.sh, and '900/771.35 = 1.167x against the worst figure anyone has measured here') were taken standalone with /usr/bin/time -p and no other load. I did NOT reproduce that method, so I am not asserting the ledger's ratio is arithmetically wrong; I am recording that a second spec is over the cap on a real host and the ledger names only one (design-review-record.test.sh at 987s, tracked as fcq3).
findings.description: runner-completeness.test.sh takes 924s through the runner on this macOS host, over the 900s per-spec cap, so make test would record it as a timeout failure here. Section 14, which this change set added, accounts for 2s of that by direct measurement, so this is pre-existing. The SPEC_TIMEOUT_S ledger names only one spec as over the cap; this is a second.

findings.evidence:
OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS ROUND, reported rather than filed as a round-7 fix, because qa-gate.sh is NOT among the 24 files of this change set -- pre-registered rule point 5.

OBSERVED while assembling this round's own review request: 'qa-gate.sh review-request-build claude-workflow-plugin-ishe --iteration 7 --stop-condition ... --spec-file ...' exited 1 with error_key=missing_completion_contract and the message 'no --completion-contract-file was given and no recorded COMPLETION v1 payload could be found for claude-workflow-plugin-ishe'. A recorded payload DOES exist and is intact: .claude/.qa-tracking/completion-claude-workflow-plugin-ishe-qa.json digests to 22e29c3be5c0bb6708c8b9d9851b05aa509a08958f4f113cf6d1bc0e1510a09f, exactly the payload_sha of the latest COMPLETION v1 record on the task.

THE CODE IS RIGHT AND THE PROSE IS NARROWER THAN THE CODE: the lookup is latest_implementer_completion_record (:8892), which deliberately excludes role=qa -- correct, and well argued in its own header. The refusal is therefore correct behaviour on a task whose implementer was the root session rather than a specialist. It is the help text at :3971-3974 and the error string at :8903 that say 'the latest recorded COMPLETION v1 payload' where the code means 'the latest recorded IMPLEMENTER payload'. Re-running with --completion-contract-file pointing at that same digest-verified payload succeeded, rc=0, 20786 bytes.

SECOND, SAME COMMAND, ALSO INFORMATIONAL: for a candidate that is already COMMITTED with a clean tree, the request's .diff is empty by construction -- it is HEAD-versus-working-tree by design, and the tool says so honestly in the field itself rather than emitting zero bytes. My review therefore read 'git diff 32b12b2 33ded0f' directly, which is the scope the brief defines.
findings.description: review-request-build's help text and its missing_completion_contract message both say 'the latest recorded COMPLETION v1 payload' where the implementation correctly looks for an IMPLEMENTER-role payload only. On a task whose implementer was the root session, that reads as 'nothing is recorded' when a valid, digest-matching payload is present. qa-gate.sh is outside this change set, so this is reported, not fixed under the round-7 rule.
